DBMS.title: Database Management Systems (DBMS) Master Cheat Sheet
DBMS.summary: Core theorems, normal forms, transaction schedules, and indexing invariants for university exams and interviews.

sections.heading: Relational Algebra & SQL Operations
sections.content:
• Selection (σ): Filters rows based on condition.
• Projection (π): Selects specific columns and eliminates duplicates in pure relational algebra.
• Cartesian Product (×): Combines every row of R with every row of S.
• Theta Join (⋈_θ): Selection over Cartesian product (σ_θ(R × S)).
• Natural Join (⋈): Equijoin over all common attribute names.
• Semi-Join (⋉): Returns tuples from R that participate in join with S.

sections.heading: Normalization Progression Checklist
sections.content:
• 1NF: Atomic values only. No repeating groups or multi-valued attributes.
• 2NF: In 1NF + No Partial Dependency (every non-prime attribute is fully functionally dependent on the whole candidate key).
• 3NF: In 2NF + No Transitive Dependency (for every X → Y, either X is a superkey OR Y is a prime attribute).
• BCNF: In 3NF + Strict: for EVERY non-trivial X → Y, X MUST be a superkey (no prime attribute exception).

sections.heading: ACID Properties & Recovery Invariants
sections.content:
• Atomicity: All or nothing execution (enforced via Undo log / Write-Ahead Logging - WAL).
• Consistency: Database transitions from one valid state to another satisfying all integrity constraints.
• Isolation: Concurrency execution is equivalent to some serial schedule (enforced via 2PL or MVCC).
• Durability: Committed updates survive system crashes (enforced via Redo log and fsync to disk).

sections.heading: B+ Tree Disk Indexing Formulas
sections.content:
• Order m: Each internal node has at most m children and at least ⌈m/2⌉ children (except root).
• Maximum keys in internal node: m - 1.
• Minimum keys in internal node: ⌈m/2⌉ - 1.
• Max Records in Leaf Node: (Block_Size - Header) / (Record_Pointer_Size + Key_Size).
• Fanout = Number of pointers per node. High fanout minimizes disk I/O seeks to 3-4 blocks.

OS.title: Operating Systems (OS) Master Cheat Sheet
OS.summary: Process state transitions, scheduling algorithms, deadlock theorems, virtual memory, and file systems.

sections.heading: Process States & Scheduling Algorithms
sections.content:
• States: New → Ready (via Long-Term Scheduler) → Running (via Dispatcher) → Terminated (or Waiting via I/O wait).
• Turnaround Time = Completion Time - Arrival Time.
• Waiting Time = Turnaround Time - Burst Time.
• Response Time = Time of first CPU allocation - Arrival Time.
• FCFS: Non-preemptive, suffers Convoy Effect.
• SJF: Optimal average waiting time, provable mathematically; suffers starvation for long jobs.
• SRTF: Preemptive version of SJF.
• Round Robin: Time quantum q. Fair, starvation-free, bounds response time.

sections.heading: Deadlock Characterization & Banker's Algorithm
sections.content:
• Coffman 4 Conditions: Mutual Exclusion, Hold & Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait.
• Prevention: Spooling (Mutual Excl), Request all at start (Hold & Wait), Preempt (No Preempt), Total ordering of resources (Circular Wait).
• Banker's Safety Algorithm:
  1. Work = Available, Finish[i] = false for all i.
  2. Find i such that Finish[i] == false and Need[i] <= Work.
  3. Work = Work + Allocation[i], Finish[i] = true. Repeat until all finish or none can.

sections.heading: Virtual Memory & Paging Hierarchy
sections.content:
• Page Size = Frame Size = 2^d bytes (d bits for offset).
• Virtual Address = Page Number (p) + Offset (d).
• Multi-Level Paging: Page directory points to second-level page tables to avoid contiguous allocation of empty tables.
• Inverted Page Table: One entry per physical frame (saves RAM, indexed via hash table on PID + VPN).
• Page Replacement: FIFO (suffers Belady's Anomaly), LRU (optimal stack algorithm), Optimal (OPT / MIN - theoretical bound).

sections.heading: Process Synchronization & Classic Concurrency
sections.content:
• Critical Section Requirements: Mutual Exclusion, Progress, Bounded Waiting.
• Peterson's Solution: 2-process software solution using flag[2] array and turn variable.
• TestAndSet / CompareAndSwap: Hardware atomic instructions.
• Semaphore: S.wait() decrements, S.signal() increments atomically.
• Classic Problems: Producer-Consumer (Bounded Buffer), Readers-Writers (Reader preference vs Writer preference), Dining Philosophers (Resource hierarchy).

DSA.title: Data Structures & Algorithms (DSA) Master Cheat Sheet
DSA.summary: Asymptotic Big-O complexities, data structure operations, graph algorithms, and DP patterns.

sections.heading: Array & Sorting Complexities
sections.content:
• Binary Search: O(log N) time, O(1) space on sorted array.
• QuickSort: O(N log N) average, O(N^2) worst (mitigated by randomized pivot).
• MergeSort: O(N log N) worst & best, stable, O(N) auxiliary space.
• HeapSort: O(N log N) worst, in-place O(1) space, not stable.

sections.heading: Graph Traversal Invariants
sections.content:
• BFS: Queue-based. O(V + E) time, O(V) space. Finds shortest path in unweighted graphs.
• DFS: Stack / recursion-based. O(V + E) time, O(V) space. Used for cycle detection and topological sorting.
• Dijkstra: Priority queue. O((V + E) log V). Non-negative edge weights only.

sections.heading: Dynamic Programming Paradigms
sections.content:
• 0/1 Knapsack: O(N * W) time & space.dp[i][w] = max(dp[i-1][w], val + dp[i-1][w - wt]).
• Longest Common Subsequence (LCS): O(M * N) time.
• Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS): O(N^2) DP or O(N log N) patience sorting with binary search.

NETWORKING.title: Computer Networks & Protocols Cheat Sheet
NETWORKING.summary: OSI and TCP/IP stack, handshake sequences, IP routing, subnet masks, and web protocols.

sections.heading: OSI vs TCP/IP Mapping
sections.content:
• Layer 7 (Application): HTTP, DNS, SMTP, SSH.
• Layer 4 (Transport): TCP (reliable, flow-controlled), UDP (datagram, low-overhead).
• Layer 3 (Network): IPv4/IPv6, ICMP, BGP, OSPF (Packets & Routing).
• Layer 2 (Data Link): Ethernet, MAC addresses, ARP, Framing (Frames).
• Layer 1 (Physical): Bits, cables, radio signals.

sections.heading: TCP Congestion Control States
sections.content:
• Slow Start: cwnd doubles every RTT until ssthresh.
• Congestion Avoidance: cwnd increases by 1 MSS per RTT (Additive Increase).
• Loss on 3 Dup ACKs: Fast Recovery (ssthresh = cwnd/2, Fast Retransmit).
• Loss on Timeout: Multiplicative Decrease (ssthresh = cwnd/2, cwnd = 1 MSS).

SYSTEM_DESIGN.title: System Design & Web Architecture Cheat Sheet
SYSTEM_DESIGN.summary: Scalability patterns, caching layers, database sharding, CAP theorem, and event-driven queues.

sections.heading: CAP Theorem & PACELC
sections.content:
• Consistency: Every read receives the most recent write.
• Availability: Every non-failing node returns a response.
• Partition Tolerance: System continues operating despite dropped network packets.
• PACELC: If Partitioned (P), choose Availability (A) or Consistency (C); Else (E), trade Latency (L) vs Consistency (C).

sections.heading: Database Sharding & Replication
sections.content:
• Horizontal Sharding: Splitting rows across databases by Shard Key (e.g. user_id % N or Range).
• Read Replicas: Master handles writes and streams binlog to asynchronous Read Slaves.
• Consistent Hashing: Minimizes key relocations upon node churn to 1/N of keys.
